clue.text: Signalling a plan for a house in the dry

indicators.note: the plan and house go inside the word for dry, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: sere means dry or withered
a map is a plan of an area

explanation.surface: Someone flags up the blueprint for a house out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MAPHO inside SERE, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a system of visual signalling with flags or arms.

clue.text: Exclusive ice cream server

definitions.meaning: a news story one paper alone has
a spoon-like utensil for serving ice cream

explanation.surface: A dedicated utensil for serving ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is both a news exclusive and a ladle for ice cream.

clue.text: Round ornament dropped initially in food for carnivore

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the food word

parts.note: a meal is food

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of dropped

parts.note: a lion is a meat-eater

explanation.surface: A medal is dropped into a predator's food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives D, which goes inside MEAL to make MEDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a round medal-like ornament.

clue.text: Stop with election about — fact or fiction?

indicators.note: the election word goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: a poll is an election

indicators.note: fiction is invented, so the letters of fact or are made up anew

explanation.surface: A vote is held about whether a story is true or false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link; 'fiction' says the letters of 'fact or' are invented anew, and 'about' wraps the election word around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A port of call is a stop on a journey.

clue.text: Veteran space traveller turned up in Lords debacle

indicators.note: the reversed traveller goes inside the anagram
a debacle is a shambles, so the letters of Lords are jumbled
in a down clue, upward means reading backwards

parts.note: ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: An alien appears in the middle of a shambles in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'debacle' makes OLDSR from LORDS, and 'turned up' reads ET upwards, since this is a down clue; 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an old person, a veteran.

clue.text: Muffler quietly placed between auditory orifices

indicators.note: the letter goes between the two ear words

parts.note: ears
lug is British slang for ear
P is the musical piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Something muffles sound, quietly fitted in the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: LUG is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An earplug muffles sound.

clue.text: Way out insect with many a substitute

indicators.note: the word for way is taken out of the insect's name, so 'out' marks a deletion

parts.note: a locust is a swarming insect
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: An exit, an insect and a crowd make an odd stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes ST from LOCUST, leaving LOCU.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in temporarily for another, a stand-in.

clue.text: Add spirit to tier

definitions.meaning: to ... a drink is to add alcohol

explanation.definitionFit: Lace means both to spike with alcohol and a cord for tying.

clue.text: Beetle to work with mouse?

explanation.definitionFit: Click is a beetle type and the act of pressing a computer mouse.

clue.text: I give reduction to Scrooge on the road to Ulster

indicators.note: the miser comes after the road

parts.note: M1 is the motorway, read as MI
NI is Northern Ireland
Scrooge is a famous miser

explanation.surface: Scrooge travels to Northern Ireland in a cost-cutting mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 motorway is read as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A minimiser makes things smaller, a reducer.

clue.text: RUC man hits hard about right to put down guns

annotationWithheld.why: RUC man hits hard about right to put down guns (5,4) for ORDER ARMS: 'put down guns' defines it and 'hits hard' gives RAMS, but no parse of 'RUC man ... about right' gives the remaining letters, and no blog or database gives the setter's intended parse.
annotationWithheld.clue: RUC man hits hard about right to put down guns

clue.text: Telling the way to go?

parts.note: reads as a description of giving instructions, but it also describes a signpost-style pointer showing the route

explanation.definitionFit: Direction means both an instruction and the way something faces or goes.

clue.text: Lovers discussing precaution — love to proceed (about time!)

parts.note: the Pill is the contraceptive precaution
love is nil, O, in tennis

indicators.note: the word for proceed sits about the time letter, so 'about' marks a container

parts.note: to walk is to proceed on foot

explanation.surface: A couple talk about contraception, impatient for things to move on at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T inside WALK to make WTALK.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillow talk is the intimate conversation of lovers in bed.

clue.text: Remove top card concealing king

indicators.note: the card holds the king inside it, so 'concealing' marks a container

parts.note: a SIM card is the chip card in a phone
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A card player palms a king while lifting the top card.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim is to take off the top layer, as cream from milk.

clue.text: Martial craft degree — split the proceeds

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: proceeds as a verb, the letters moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Graduates divide the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proceeds' rearranges SPLITTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleship is a warship, a martial vessel.

clue.text: Transport blended to give Lara some cricket?

indicators.note: the letters are mixed together to produce the answer, so this marks an anagram

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only part of the word cricket is used, so 'some' marks a hidden run

explanation.surface: Brian Lara, the West Indies batsman, is offered some cricket by a mixed-up mode of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes CRI from cricket; 'blended to give' mixes LARA and CRI. The clue reads backwards too: the answer blended gives Lara and some cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcar is a self-propelled railway carriage, a form of transport.

clue.text: Line includes one sort of word for Ratty's home

indicators.note: the line word contains the others

parts.note: a rank is a line
I is the Roman numeral one
a verb is a part of speech

explanation.surface: A line with one particular word sets up Ratty's dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty is the Water Rat in The Wind in the Willows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty lives on the riverbank.

clue.text: Looks good with 24

parts.note: 24 is arms, and lances are arms or weapons

explanation.surface: Appearances are improved by weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to the answer of 24-down, ARMS; lances are a kind of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Glances are quick looks, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Dishonest mason?

parts.note: a stoneworker uses a chisel, and a cheat chisels people

explanation.definitionFit: A chiseller is a cheat, as well as someone using a chisel.

clue.text: Transport reported not so good — pods needed

parts.note: a van is a means of transport

indicators.note: the word is heard rather than spelt, so 'reported' marks a homophone

parts.note: iller means worse in health, not so good

explanation.surface: A vehicle reported as worse off needs replacement parts.
explanation.walkthrough: ILLER said aloud sounds like ILLA in a non-rhotic accent. The definition is loose: vanilla comes from pods.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla flavouring comes from the long seed pods of a climbing orchid.

clue.text: First to prevent crossing

parts.note: A is first
thwart means prevent

explanation.surface: The first plan to stop a crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: athwart is an old preposition meaning across or from side to side of something.

clue.text: I keep mum? On the contrary, I'm rather bug-infested

indicators.note: keeping suggests one thing holds another, marking a container
reverses the roles: mum keeps I rather than I keeping mum

parts.note: mum means mother

explanation.surface: Someone keeps quiet, then admits to being riddled with insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I keep mum' would put MOTHER inside I; 'On the contrary' flips it so MOTHER holds I. 'Keep mum' means stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothier means more full of moths, insects that infest cloth.

clue.text: Camphor gives people time for a break

parts.note: men are people
T is time
hol is short for holiday

explanation.surface: Camphor gives people time for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Menthol is a camphor-like compound.

clue.text: Value speed?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a speed, as in a ... of knots

explanation.definitionFit: Rate means both to assess worth and a pace or speed of movement.

clue.text: You need to talk — in part? The lot!

indicators.note: only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: Someone needs to talk the whole thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the total is the whole amount, every last item counted together.

clue.text: The game's about keeping the spirit intact

indicators.note: the game goes around the spirit, holding it within, marking a container

parts.note: chess is the game; the 's is just the verb
an angel is a spirit

explanation.surface: A game that holds onto its spirit remains whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The game's' is the game plus 'is'; the surface suggests a spirit intact, but 'the spirit' is a heavenly being.
explanation.definitionFit: Changeless means unaltered, as something intact is.

clue.text: Bring up guns: sergeant-major's about to see fruit

indicators.note: the sergeant-major letters go around

parts.note: SM is sergeant-major, plus S
lo means look
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Sergeant-major sees fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Slope arms is a drill command.
explanation.definitionFit: Slope arms means bring rifles up to the shoulder.

clue.text: See 9 and 23
Consequence of a dad almost without limit

indicators.note: here means outside, the dad's letters around the limit
the word for dad is cut short, so 'almost' marks a deletion

parts.note: dad means father
a term is a limit or end

explanation.surface: Something comes of a father almost boundless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the father word to FATH, losing its last two letters; 'without' is the old sense outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftermath is the consequences following an event.

clue.text: Greeting from old saint (detail)

indicators.note: de-tail: the last letter is removed, marking a deletion

parts.note: hallow is an old word for a saint, as in All Hallows

explanation.surface: A hello comes from a saint, with a small extra point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' is read as de-tail, removing W from HALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallo is a variant of hello, a greeting.

clue.text: Book ends at length — in Irish town

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word book is used

parts.note: ells are old measures of length for cloth

explanation.surface: A book finishes its long run in an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' also hints at the Book of Kells, the illuminated manuscript once kept in the town of Kells.
explanation.definitionFit: Kells is a town in County Meath, Ireland.

clue.text: Bad lie — putter used — big bloomer

indicators.note: a bad lie in golf; here the letters are made bad, scrambled

explanation.surface: A golfer has an awkward lie and the putter is pressed into service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' mixes LIE and PUTTER together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tulip tree is a large flowering tree, a jokey big bloomer.
